key_insight: SolCloudLLM improves short-term solar power and irradiance forecasting by fusing sky images with time-series data through bidirectional multimodal alignment for an LLM-based predictor.
engineering_relevance: Better cloud-ramp anticipation can improve PV dispatch, reserve scheduling, and grid operations, especially at sites with limited historical data.
method: Align sky-image patches with time-series patches.
Fuse both modalities bidirectionally into a unified representation.
Map the fused embedding into an LLM for forecasting.
evidence_signal: On the SIRTA and SKIPP'D datasets, the method outperformed all baselines in MSE across forecast horizons, with up to 25.4% relative MSE reduction and strong few-shot performance, especially under cloudy conditions.
watch_item: The approach likely depends on site-specific sky imagery and careful multimodal data alignment, which may limit deployment where image coverage or calibration is poor.
paper_title: Bidirectional Multimodal Fusion of Sky Images and Time-Series for Solar Forecasting with Large Language Models
